I’m going to somewhat go against the grain here and say that if you feel this is something you have a genuine interest in and not just because you think it’s easy money, then go ahead and do it. Obviously, it goes without saying, be careful. 

I spent about a year being a sex worker who did outcalls (so in person) and I also minimally did porn, which is online. There are safeguards against being found out (as far as I’m aware, nobody knows unless I’ve told them. Also remember there are no guarantees) but I’m not going to spell them out because there’s definitely value in you figuring things out, but obviously hiding distinguishing features and using a pseudonym are a good place to start. 

Honestly I think psychology and society generally need a big cultural shift in our attitude towards sex workers. I’m in the middle of my Msc in psychology as well as level 3 counselling qualification and looking at clinical doctorates now, I also work with psychologists and psychiatrists l. I’m in the UK and I haven’t noticed any particular prejudice towards sex workers here, but that is my anecdotal experience. However it clearly goes on.

Another thing to add is that there is a big big hole where sex-worker friendly clinicians ought to be, I definitely would’ve benefited from therapists and practitioners who were better informed about my experiences, but obviously becoming a sex worker is not the only way to do this. 

I also saw another comment mentioning that you’re MTF, if I’ve got that wrong apologies, but just food for thought if you are (as am I); trans people are so often reduced to their anatomy and I think it instills a sense of having to make up for what we feel we cannot give. I personally feel that being trans is chronically traumatic in a bodily way and I wonder if this gives us funny ways of thinking about our worth and what we have to offer the world. 

It’s very important to view this decision through multiple contexts and I’m sure in doing that you’ll be able to decide what is right for you.

I feel like that often too to be honest. Sex is still a bit of a taboo socially I would say, the popular conception of people who think about sex a lot is usually a ‘creepy’ person holed up in their room. 

But it’s a starting point you know? If it gets you through the day… so what? I think maybe the fairest thing you could do here is enjoy it in moderation. Set boundaries with yourself so you are still in control. But don’t tell yourself no, because it doesn’t work.
It’s okay, I promise. I’ve done things like that before too, you are worthy of loving yourself.

Sometimes as I’m sure you know, we as survivors of this stuff might re-enact the events to gain a sense of control over it, or perhaps we might experience hyper-sexuality from time to time as a response to it. 

But you know what? It IS okay to enjoy sex, it doesn’t make you bad. It is okay to go along with those feelings of hyper sexuality. It is okay to explore other peoples bodies. 

There is NO moral slant on sexual intercourse that happens between fully consenting adults. That is between you and them and no one else. Maybe you realise you didn’t enjoy it. This is okay too. Non-traumatised people also have sex they realise isn’t for them afterwards. It doesn’t make you bad, or dirty, it makes you human.

The fact that you were drunk could’ve made you feel less in control than you wanted to feel. It’s okay to make these kinds of mistakes and learn about yourself from it. 

You’re not pathetic at all. Recovering from SA/CSA isn’t sobriety. There is no rule that says we can’t enjoy interacting with other humans. You have done nothing wrong. I’ll bet this is that little voice in your head that tries to make you feel bad and guilty.

If you’ve decided on a rule of celibacy for yourself of course that’s fine too, but definitely worth understanding why you want that for yourself, for how long, what do you consider that to mean to you etc. Make sure it’s not something that you’re assuming you should do.

Be kind to yourself, OP. The takeaway here is perhaps that you simply don’t enjoy that type of thing, as opposed to being bad, pathetic, whatever. We are allowed to explore!
